speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your appointment, I can see you are here for chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort. To begin our evaluation, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and have there been any episodes of blood or black tarry stools?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Infectious colitis (likely Campylobacter or E. coli given the camping history) or Inflammatory Bowel Disease (UC). The symptom of relief after defecation and mucus discharge strongly suggests an inflammatory process. Given the camping history with a sick companion, an infectious etiology is high on the differential. I will request stool studies to confirm infection. REQUEST TEST: Stool_Culture_and_Sensitivity, REQUEST TEST: Stool_Ova_and_Parasites, REQUEST TEST: Fecal_Calprotectin.
